title: Sesotho Introduction ordinary-clause candidate supplement: mark, rotation, distance/frequency, older neighbour

lexicalEvidence.source: DBE Sesotho HL P2 May–June 2019 Memo, answer-marking instruction, lines 11–15 and 25–27 of opened PDF
lexicalEvidence.scopeLimit: Official use supports the lexical action mark in answer marking. It is not direct evidence of fluent map/house/zone phrasing.

lexicalEvidence.source: DSAC Multilingual Mathematics Dictionary 2013 search result, Sesotho equivalent for draw
lexicalEvidence.scopeLimit: Search result only; PDF open returned internal error. Used only to distinguish the established draw verb from the proposed mark verb.

rows.sourceEnglish: Draw your boundary. Mark the house. Draw the rings outward by how often you visit.
rows.currentTarget: Draw your boundary. Mark the house. Draw the rings outward by how often you visit.
rows.fullProposedTarget: Thala moedi wa hao. Tshwaya ntlo. Thala rings ho ya kantle ho latela hore na o etela hangata hakae.
rows.backTranslation: Draw your boundary. Mark the house. Draw rings outward according to how often you visit.
rows.reason: Use thala for draw and tshwaya for mark, preserving the distinct actions. Keep rings as an English graphic term and preserve outward direction and the visit-frequency relation. Official DBE Sesotho examination instructions use tshwaya for mark (in answer-marking context); the lexical action is supported, while no claim is made that the full house-map phrase has local review.

rows.sourceEnglish: Mark Zone 0 and Zone 1 first, then work outward as far as your land goes.
rows.currentTarget: Mark Zone 0 and Zone 1 first, then work outward as far as your land goes.
rows.fullProposedTarget: Tshwaya Zone 0 le Zone 1 pele, ebe o tswela kantle ho fihlela moo setsha sa hao se fellang teng.
rows.backTranslation: Mark Zone 0 and Zone 1 first, then go outward as far as your site ends.
rows.reason: Use tshwaya to preserve mark rather than changing the instruction into draw. Preserve both named zones, first/then order, outward work, and the site extent. Retain Zone labels exactly.

rows.sourceEnglish: A garden, fruit trees and a chicken run arranged so the chickens rotate through the beds after harvest is integration. Keep chickens away from crops being harvested for food. Fresh manure can carry germs. Ask an extension adviser how to manage the bed safely before edible crops return. The chickens can clean up pests and add fertility instead of sitting idle in a fixed pen.
rows.currentTarget: A garden, fruit trees and a chicken run arranged so the chickens rotate through the beds after harvest is integration. Keep chickens away from crops being harvested for food. Fresh manure can carry germs. Ask an extension adviser how to manage the bed safely before edible crops return. The chickens can clean up pests and add fertility instead of sitting idle in a fixed pen.
rows.fullProposedTarget: Serapa, difate tsa ditholwana le chicken run di hlophisitswe hore dikgoho rotate through the beds after harvest — hoo ke integration. Boloka dikgoho hole le dijalo tse kotulwang bakeng sa dijo. Manyoro a foreshe a ka jara germs. Kopa extension adviser hore a o bolelle kamoo bed e laolwa ka polokeho pele dijalo tse jewang di kgutla. Dikgoho di ka clean up pests le ho eketsa fertility ho ena le ho dula di sa sebetse ka pen e sa fetoheng.
rows.backTranslation: A garden, fruit trees and chicken run are arranged so chickens rotate through the beds after harvest — that is integration. Keep chickens away from crops being harvested for food. Fresh manure can carry germs. Ask an extension adviser to tell you how the bed is managed safely before edible crops return. Chickens can clean up pests and add fertility instead of sitting idle in a fixed pen.
rows.reason: Localize the arrangement, crop exclusion, fresh-manure possibility, request to the adviser, safe-bed management, before-return timing, and final instead-of relation. Retain chicken run, rotate through the beds after harvest, integration, germs, bed, clean up pests, fertility, and pen as technical/context-sensitive anchors. This avoids the unsupported prior “empty bed” interpretation; it does not claim a locally reviewed way to translate rotation or pest-cleanup.

rows.sourceEnglish: Find one thing planted further away than how often you use it, and write down where it should move to.
rows.currentTarget: Find one thing planted further away than how often you use it, and write down where it should move to.
rows.fullProposedTarget: Fumana ntho e le nngwe e lenngweng further away than how often you use it, mme o ngole moo e lokelang ho iswa teng.
rows.backTranslation: Find one thing planted further away than how often you use it, and write where it should be moved to.
rows.reason: Translate find one planted thing and write down where it should move, preserving one and should. Retain the source’s unusual distance-versus-frequency comparison verbatim rather than inventing a measurement or changing it to distance from the user.

rows.sourceEnglish: Then ask one older neighbour which direction the worst wind comes from, and compare their answer with your arrow.
rows.currentTarget: Then ask one older neighbour which direction the worst wind comes from, and compare their answer with your arrow.
rows.fullProposedTarget: Ebe o botse moahisani a le mong ya moholo hore na worst wind e tswa ka lehlakoreng lefe, mme o bapise karabo ya hae le motsu wa hao.
rows.backTranslation: Then ask one older neighbour which direction the worst wind comes from, and compare their answer with your arrow.
rows.reason: Translate then, ask, one, older neighbour, which direction it comes from, and compare the answer to your arrow. Retain worst wind as an exact-English anchor because translating worst as strongest or most damaging could change the requested category. Preserve the sequencing, count, source direction, and comparison.

rows.sourceEnglish: You plant herbs in Zone 3, the main field far from the house. What problem does this create?
rows.currentTarget: U byala herbs eka Zone 3, main field leyi nga ekule na yindlu. Xana leswi swi vanga xiphiqo xihi?
rows.originalAuditCurrentTarget: U byala herbs eka Zone 3, main field leyi nga ekule na yindlu. Xana leswi swi vanga xiphiqo xihi?

rows.exclusionReason: Keep “main field” as the exact source category; do not let the existing Tshivenda “main” idea become size without review.

rows.sourceEnglish: Put a crop you pick often near a daily path. A distant bed adds walking and may be checked less often.
rows.currentTarget: Vheani tshimela tshine na tshi ka lunzhi tsini ha nḓila ya ḓuvha ḽiṅwe na ḽiṅwe. Bed i re kule i engedza u tshimbila nahone i nga tolwa less often.

rows.sourceEnglish: First find out if sharing is allowed. Check whether the borehole can serve all users without taking too much. If sharing is allowed and there is enough water, agree how to share fairly and keep watching the water level. People Care and Fair Share guide the agreement. Earth Care means protecting the source. Watching the level alone does not make extra use safe or allowed.
rows.currentTarget: Thomani nga u wana arali u kovhelana ho tendelwa. Ṱolani arali borehole i nga kona u shumela vhashumisi vhoṱhe hu si na u dzhia maḓi manzhi lwo kalaho. Arali u kovhelana ho tendelwa nahone hu na maḓi o eḓanaho, tendelanani uri ni kovhelane nga ndinganyo ni dzule ni tshi sedza vhuimo ha maḓi. People Care na Fair Share zwi livhisa u tendelana. Earth Care zwi amba u tsireledza tshiko. U sedza vhuimo ha maḓi fhedzi a zwi ambi uri u shumisa maḓi o engedzeaho zwi safe kana zwo tendelwa.
